page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword.

main_text.p: us annumerat Lib. III. errorum po- ularium cap. 2. Sententiam, quâ qui bile carere dicuntur. quando- uidem, inquit, beneficio anatomiae se invenisse membranosam quan- am substantiam extrinsecus albican- cm intrinsecus felleam. ego duplici facta experientia pelliculam illam re- eri primum humore subacido, dein- e humore biliofo cum acido tempe- ato refertam. quae cum ductu he- atico sese exonerabant in ductum communem, in quem itidem humor cidulus ex pancreate profluebat, at- ue inde in intestinum duodenum, ut iliosus humor eo loci facta primum fervescentia temperaretur, uti supra liquoties significatum. Admirabar magnitudinem hujus ductus commu- is, utpote qui digitum auricularem acile capiebat, cujus magnitudini ariter respondebant ductus bilarius ommunis atque pancreaticus: capa- itas horum ductuum prohibent ne gene-

page.notes: The left edge of the page is cut off, so the first lines begin with fragments of words (us, ularium, qui, uidem, se, am, cm, facta, eri, e, ato, atico, ommunem, cidulus, ue, iliosus, fervescentia, liquoties, magnitudinem, is, acile, ariter, ommunis, itas); these are left as fragments. The first line reads "Lib. III." as printed in small capitals. The word at the start of the eighth line is partly hidden and was read as "facta". The last line "gene-" is right-aligned and carries a printed hyphen; it was read as text, not as a catchword.
